rule.description: A production unit fires when its own body embeds the low-level container mechanics that the decomposed library keeps inside its collection-helper types (stack, priority queue, layered stacks, union-find): two or more distinct embedded idiom families, or one idiom family together with at least 40 direct statements. Nested function literals are measured as separate units, so extracting the absorbed mechanics back into a helper, closure, or type clears a report.

checks.description: Detect traversal and exploration loops that embed the shared stack helper's pop mechanics: the end-truncating slice assignment together with the membership-registry insert/evict pair that the helper's push and pop perform.
checks.detected_relation: unit -> inlined body of collection.stack push/pop mechanics
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The stack type still exists in collection.go for its direct tests, but these four consumers no longer delegate to it; the sub-abstraction's implementation has been copied into each caller's own body.

matches.evidence: drives the DFS walk over a pending slice: `pending = pending[:len(pending)-1]`, `delete(onPending, current)` alongside `onPending[...] = struct{}{}` inserts.
ancestor walk over an ancestors slice: `ancestors = ancestors[:len(ancestors)-1]`, `delete(queued, currentHash)` alongside `queued[adjacency] = struct{}{}` inserts.
traversal loop over a frontier slice: `frontier = frontier[:len(frontier)-1]`, `delete(queued, currentHash)` alongside `queued[adjacency] = struct{}{}` inserts.

open-trail machine over a trail slice: `trail = trail[:len(trail)-1]`, `delete(trailMembers, popped)` alongside `trailMembers[...] = struct{}{}` inserts, alongside the parallel frame/cursor/successor stacks it retreats with plain index truncations.

layer discipline over the path and layers slices: `path = path[:len(path)-1]` and `layers = layers[:len(layers)-1]`, `delete(onPath, current)` alongside `onPath[element] = struct{}{}` inserts, with the removed stackOfStacks guard errors kept in the body.

checks.description: Detect relaxation loops that embed the priorityQueue helper's internals: container/heap operations and priorityItem construction outside collection.go, coupled with the insert/evict bookkeeping of the helper's item cache map.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: ShortestPath previously delegated its agenda to the priorityQueue helper; it now drives the binary heap and the cache map with the same primitive operations the helper encapsulates.

matches.evidence: relaxation loop over a local minHeap: `heap.Push(&items, item)` with a literal `&priorityItem[K]{...}`, `heap.Pop(&items).(*priorityItem[K])`, `heap.Fix(&items, relax.index)`, and `delete(onHeap, item.value)` alongside `onHeap[hash] = item` inserts.

checks.description: Detect construction loops that embed the unionFind helper's find body: self-parent chain marches over the parents map, whose insert/evict pair is absent here, so the unit fires through the chain-marching idiom combined with the absorbed statement volume.
checks.detected_relation: unit -> inlined body of sets.unionFind add/find/union mechanics
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: spanningTree previously tracked subtree membership through the unionFind helper; it now performs root walks, entry-key path compression, and subtree joins directly over the subtrees map while also assembling the target graph inline.

matches.evidence: component loop over the subtrees map with two self-parent marches `for subtrees[sourceSubtree] != sourceSubtree` / `for subtrees[targetSubtree] != targetSubtree`, inline path compression, inline graph assembly replacing the NewLike constructor chain, inline property copying, and a literal AddEdge option replacing copyEdge.

excluded.candidate: collection.go stack.push/stack.pop and sets.go unionFind.find bodies (one idiom, under 40 direct statements)
excluded.reason: These are the helper implementations the absorbed fragments were copied from; the rule leaves legitimate small helper bodies alone.

excluded.candidate: production units of the clean baseline with >= 40 direct statements
excluded.reason: The largest legit unit in the decomposed baseline measures 35 direct statements and carries none of the embedded idiom families, so length alone cannot fire the rule.
Queue and slice bookkeeping without log/registry or heap idiom co-location; these units do not embed any helper mechanics.
